sections.h2: Where is Watertown, MA, and how is the city laid out?
sections.html:
Watertown is a small, dense city in Middlesex County, just west of Boston and Cambridge. The Census count was 35,329 in 2020, packed into roughly four square miles, which works out to about 8,840 people per square mile.

The Charles River forms much of its southern and eastern edge toward Boston's Brighton neighborhood. Belmont sits to the north, Newton to the south, Cambridge to the east and Waltham to the west. Most of the city lies north of the river, but the line crosses it near Watertown Square to take in the streets around Casey Playground.

Neighborhood names you will hear in listings and from neighbors include Bemis, Coolidge Square, East Watertown, Watertown Square and the West End. Mount Auburn Cemetery, which covers 151.1 acres, is mostly inside Watertown even though people think of it as a Cambridge landmark.

sections.h2: What is Watertown's history, and why does it matter for an older house?
sections.html:
Watertown was settled in 1630 as one of the earliest Massachusetts Bay Colony towns, so a house here can sit on land that has been built on for nearly four centuries. Many sellers hold homes that went up when the city was a streetcar suburb of Boston.

Two chapters shaped the modern city. The Watertown Arsenal made military armaments from 1816 until 1995, when the Army sold the site. It has since turned into offices, shops, restaurants and the Mosesian Center for the Arts. Along Arsenal Street you now find Arsenal Yards and the Watertown Mall facing each other.

Watertown is also home to the third-largest Armenian community in the country, according to Wikipedia, with newspapers, churches and grocery stores concentrated around East Watertown. Voters changed the official name to "The City of Watertown" in November 2021.

sections.h2: How do people get around Watertown, and does it affect a sale?
sections.html:
Bus service runs through Watertown Square and Watertown Yard, and the Massachusetts Turnpike and Soldiers Field Road run along its edges toward downtown Boston. The Green Line's A branch used to reach the city but stopped in 1969.

A buyer looking at a Watertown house will usually ask three transport questions:

  • How far is the nearest MBTA bus stop?
  • How long is the drive to the Pike or Soldiers Field Road at rush hour?
  • Is there off-street parking, which is scarce on tight city lots?

If you plan to list, answer those up front. If you take a cash offer, a buyer who plans to renovate cares much less about them.

sections.h2: Which schools and employers shape Watertown housing demand?
sections.html:
Watertown Public Schools serve about 2,600 students through three elementary schools, one middle school and Watertown High School. Private options named on Wikipedia include the Perkins School, St. Stephen's Armenian Elementary School and the Atrium School.

Wikipedia lists Perkins School for the Blind, Exergen, Tufts Health Plan, NESN, Vanasse Hangen Brustlin and athenahealth among employers based in the city. The Arsenal campus was bought by Alexandria Real Estate Equities in 2019, adding to life science development along Arsenal Street. Boston and Cambridge sit right next door, so many residents commute out rather than work in the city.

sections.h2: How does Massachusetts property tax work for a Watertown seller?
sections.html:
Property tax in Watertown follows state law, and the Massachusetts Appellate Tax Board explains the steps in a public guide. Assessors value property as of January 1 before the fiscal year, so a bill for fiscal 2025 reflects value on January 1, 2024.

Where a city bills quarterly, installments are generally due August 1, November 1, February 1 and May 1. A city that bills twice a year usually sets the due date thirty days after mailing. Check the front of your actual bill to see which schedule applies, because the due date for an abatement request is tied to it.

  • An abatement application goes to the local assessors on or before the first installment due date, usually February 1 for quarterly billing.
  • Assessors have three months to act. If they do nothing, the application is deemed denied after three calendar months.
  • An appeal to the Appellate Tax Board must follow within three months of that action or deemed denial.
  • Taxes must be paid on time for the board to hear the case.

Watertown's assessing office posts its own calendar and forms, so confirm the current dates and the abatement form with that office before you rely on any date here.

sections.h2: What does a deed transfer cost when a Watertown house sells?
sections.html:
The seller normally pays the Massachusetts deed excise tax, which is $2.28 for each $500 of consideration or fraction of it. The Norfolk County Registry of Deeds gives an example: a $155,000 deed carries $706.80 in excise tax, paid with an attorney's check or bank check at recording.

Watertown is in Middlesex County, and the registry that records its deeds posts its own fee schedule. The Norfolk and Hampden registries list a deed recording fee of $156 and $155, so expect something close, and confirm the exact figure with the Middlesex registry. The statute, G.L. c. 64D, section 1, sets the tax and exempts deeds to which a city, town or the state is a party.

sections.h2: What should a Watertown owner ask the city before selling?
sections.html:
City rules change, and a few topics are best confirmed with the offices directly. Ask these questions before you list or sign a sale agreement:

  • Are there open permits, violations or unpaid municipal charges on the property?
  • Does the city require any inspection or certificate for a sale or a change of occupancy?
  • If tenants live there, what notice and registration rules apply?
  • What are the tax payment dates on your current bill?

Anything unresolved can slow a traditional sale and may reduce what a buyer is willing to pay. A cash buyer purchasing as-is often takes the house with these items still open, with the price reflecting them.

sections.h2: Listing, selling on your own, or taking a cash offer in Watertown
sections.html:
A listing can reach the widest pool of buyers, but it usually means repairs, showings and a closing timeline set by a buyer's lender. A cash sale is faster and simpler, and the price typically reflects the work the house needs.

For a Watertown owner dealing with an inherited house, a vacant property, tenants or deferred repairs, the useful comparison is the net amount after commission, repairs and carrying costs over the weeks a listing might take. Compare that against a written cash offer, and read any contract carefully before you sign.

faqs.q: Is Watertown, MA a city or a town?
faqs.a: Watertown is a city. It runs under a council-manager form of government, and voters changed the official name to "The City of Watertown" in November 2021.
Watertown covers about 4.12 square miles, and the 2020 Census counted 35,329 residents.

faqs.q: How much is the deed excise tax when I sell a house in Watertown?
faqs.a: It is $2.28 for every $500 of the price, or fraction of $500. On a $500,000 sale that works out to $2,280.

faqs.q: How do I challenge my Watertown property tax assessment?
faqs.a: File an abatement application with the city's assessors by the first installment due date on your bill, then appeal to the state Appellate Tax Board within three months of the assessors' decision if you disagree. Pay the bill on time throughout.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Watertown house that needs major repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. You can list it as is, sell it to an investor, or accept a cash offer from a company that buys as is. Unpaid taxes and liens are settled from the sale proceeds at closing.
